findings: Reward coins collected immediately instead of remaining available.
Dropping through a deck could skip the next deck.
Attract player could stall below the central boss seal.
Enemy metadata overwrote event categories, losing sound and effects.
String replacement corrupted the bundled inline JavaScript.
Guest results could use a stale final host snapshot.
Attract restart logic existed in both the game and UI loop.
Returning from result credits could open a frozen gameplay screen.
Quick keyboard taps could be lost between frames.
Generic font fallback edits invalidated the embedded font-face family.
Instance colors multiplied the wall tint twice, obscuring brick detail.
Deck bump state was not connected to the rendered deck motion.
Room-code text entry was not usable with only a gamepad.
Menu/game input state changed one frame after the screen changed.
The software WebGPU device was lost; rendering needed automatic canvas/backend recovery.
GPU restart reset accelerated 2D label canvases, erasing world labels.
Kick animation direction did not follow player facing.
Standalone replay dropped the network connection and became local co-op.
A disconnected buddy remained vulnerable and could consume shared lives.
Compressed seat arrays after a departure could route inputs to the wrong actor.
A departed actor could respawn on the next phase.
Guests did not receive the host’s action sounds, effects and music phase changes.
Startup tutorial and toast overlays could cover the keeper on the ground.
Held controls did not inhibit idle attract, and the right stick was not counted as input.
The boss pressure seals were obscured by the front of the top bridge.
